3. The plaintiff's case, in short, inter-alia, is that Fazlu Miah was the recorded owner of 10.26 acres of land, in PS Khatian No.1041 under Mouja Char Jublee within Police Station Sadar, District Noakhali. After his death his only son, Hossain Ahamed Kazi inherited the same and mortgaged the same to Mohammad Miah, predecessor of defendant Nos. 2 to 4, at Taka 130 by a conditional sale deed executed and registered on 20th Chaitra 1341 BS for a period of 8 years on condition, to repay the aforesaid money within 20th Chaitra 1349 BS and get back the said land. But Hossain Ahamed Kazi did not redeem it. While Mohammad Hossain Miah was owner in possession of the said land, none paid the government taxes and, as such, the suit land was put into auction and the government purchased the same on 1-10-1936 in Certificate Case No. 201 of 1933-34 which was confirmed on 4-12-1936. Thus, the Government became the owner of the said land. The said Mohammad Hossain Miah then took settlement of said land in Revenue Settlement Case No.650 of 1936-37 from the Government and accordingly, SA Khatian No. 2594 was opened in his name and since then he had been enjoying the suit land. Subsequently, the land was correctly recorded in his name in Diara Khatian No. 2336. After the death of Mohammad Hossain Miah his heirs, defendant Nos. 2-4 sold the suit land to the plaintiffs by four kabalas all dated 25-3-1974 and delivered possession of the same to the transferees. But subsequently, the suit land was wrongly recorded in Khatian No.1 in the name of the Government and, as such, the local Tahsilder on 4-11-1974 refused to accept the rent from the plaintiffs. Thus, they were constrained to institute the suit. 

 11. Mr. Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate-on Record appearing on behalf of the respondent No.2 submits that both the Courts below without applying their judicial mind and upon non reading and misreading the materials on record came to an erroneous decision and thereby, dismissed the suit which the High Court Division upon full consideration of the materials on record set aside by the impugned judgment and order. According to him, PW 1 proved the Kabuliat submitted by the Government as Exhibit 4 showing that the plaintiffs got the settlement of the suit land from the Government, and they are possessing and enjoying the same without any hindrance. All the PWs, according to him, categorically proved the plaintiffs' possession in the suit land during the SA settlement and their names have been rightly prepared and published in the SA Khatian as Exhibit 1(ICa). He submits that the defendant No.1, the Government, claimed that the suit land was diluvion land which was under the water for long time and, as such, the plaintiffs' predecessor lost his title and possession over the suit land as no claim was ever made within the specific period. Such finding of the Courts below was totally misreading of materials on record inasmuch as had it been so the SA Khatian would never have been prepared in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiffs. He submits that no evidence has been led by the defendants to prove that the suit land was under water and, as such, the submissions of the defendants are totally wrong. He submits that the Courts below failed to consider that PW 1 proved the rent receipt (Exhibit 5) produced by the plaintiffs and also failed to consider and determine the possession of the plaintiffs although all the PWs categorically proved the same and the documents exhibited by the plaintiffs in support of their title and possession clearly proves their title and possession in the suit land by constructing houses and living there. Hence the findings of the courts below were erroneous. In support of his submission he relied on the case of Md. Nurul Islam vs Bangladesh, reported in 17 BLD (AD) 91 = 2 BLC (AD) 56; and thereby submitted that since construction of document is a mixed question of law and fact and the same having not properly been construed by the Courts below, the High Court Division was very much within its competence to reverse the said finding of fact arrived at by the Courts below giving cogent reason. He submits that the courts below failed to take into consideration Exhibit 1(Ka), S.A Khatian, Kabuliyat (Exhibit 4) and the rent receipt (Exhibit 5) which obviously proved the plaintiffs' right, title and possession in the suit land. The High Court Division having considered those documents found that the plaintiffs have been able to prove their right, title and possession in the suit land and made the Rule absolute by the impugned judgment. Lastly relying on the decision in the case of Hossain Ahmed Chowdhury vs Mr. Nurul Amin, reported in 47 DLR (AD) 162; Mr. Bhuiyan submits that when there is misreading of evidence and non consideration of some material evidence then it was incumbent on the revisional court to consider the same and to arrive at a proper finding on the material evidence on record and to finally dispose of the case. Thus the High Court Division has rightly made the Rule absolute which does not call for any interference by this Court.
